title: The Legend of Zelda: Phantom Hourglass

nodes.name: Stylus input, steering and gesture recognition
nodes.purpose: Samples the touchscreen, maps the stylus to a world-plane offset, decides tap and hold goals, and turns strokes into sword swings and aim points.

nodes.name: Player state handlers, interaction and equipment
nodes.purpose: Holds the character state machine: movement, damage reactions, grabbing, pushing, throwing, and the hammer charge and swing timing.

nodes.name: Actor bodies, gravity and floor contact
nodes.purpose: Base actor with position, velocity, gravity, fall cap, cylinder hitbox, floor snapping and a near or far activity class.

nodes.name: Combat contact, shield and damage reactions
nodes.purpose: Resolves sword, shield, hammer and roll contacts, picks a reaction level per incoming object, and applies knockback, damage windows and respawn.

nodes.name: Map grid, floor heights and room camera viewpoints
nodes.purpose: Serves the one-unit tile grid, per-tile floor heights and the authored camera viewpoint table used to frame each room.

cards.name: Stylus position to world-plane offset
cards.summary: The last stylus position maps to a world-plane offset from the screen centre; the screen vertical axis becomes world depth
cards.behavior: Steering reads the stylus, not an analogue stick. While the stylus is touching, the last touch position is turned into a world offset from the screen centre (128, 96 pixels): the horizontal pixel offset is scaled so that the 256 pixel screen width spans 10.625 world units, and the vertical pixel offset is scaled so that the 192 pixel screen height spans the same 10.625 units. That gives about 0.0415 world units per pixel sideways and 0.0553 per pixel up or down, and the screen vertical axis becomes world depth (z) with height zero. The offset is the base for the aim vector and the aim point of items. The offset is only produced while a touch is active. The header comment for the distance field says there is a dead zone of 20 pixels around the character, but the code in this file does not use 20; the distance checks that exist use 10, 16 and 24 pixels in other cards.

constants.name: Horizontal centre of the touchscreen
constants.unit: pixels from the left edge, touch position sampled per update, rate unverified

constants.name: Vertical centre of the touchscreen
constants.unit: pixels from the top edge, touch position sampled per update, rate unverified

constants.name: World span of the full screen width and height
constants.unit: world units spanned by 256 pixels horizontally and by 192 pixels vertically, static mapping

cards.name: Stylus distance to movement-speed fraction
cards.summary: Speed is the square of stylus distance over an 80-pixel reference, softened during the first four updates of a contact.
cards.behavior: The character has a continuous speed fraction rather than a fixed walk. While a touch is active, the stylus distance from the character in pixels is divided by 80 and the quotient is squared, so a distance of 40 pixels gives a quarter of the speed, 60 pixels gives about 56 percent, and 80 pixels or more gives the full fraction. While the contact is younger than four updates the fraction is reduced by a quarter for each update still missing, so tapping far from the character does not start at full speed. A negative result becomes zero and the fraction is clamped to one. With no active touch the fraction is zero, unless a held-button flag is set, in which case it is one.

constants.name: Reference stylus distance for full speed
constants.unit: pixels between stylus and character, per update, rate unverified

constants.name: Ramp length at the start of a contact
constants.unit: updates of the touch state, per update, rate unverified

constants.name: Upper clamp of the speed fraction
constants.unit: dimensionless fraction of the walk speed, per update, rate unverified

cards.name: Tap and short hold to approach
cards.summary: A contact that ends within 20 updates and 10 pixels of the recorded drag point selects a follow goal; a follow with no progress for 15 updates is dropped
cards.behavior: A tap is a contact that ends when its duration is under 21 updates, provided the release point is within 10 pixels of the recorded fast-drag point. On a tap the engine uses the nearest actor picked under the stylus when there is one and otherwise a map point under the stylus. That target becomes a follow goal and a stuck timer of 15 starts. A separate check accepts a contact of 15 to 29 updates on the last tapped actor. While following, the distance to the goal is compared with the value from the previous update. Progress of 0.01 world units or less counts down the stuck timer, and when it reaches zero the follow stops. After a cutscene ends, a 15-update timer must run out before a tap is accepted again.

constants.name: Contact duration bound for a tap
constants.unit: updates, exclusive upper bound, per update, rate unverified

constants.name: Squared tap radius around the drag start
constants.unit: square pixels, equal to a 10 pixel radius, checked once on release

constants.name: Hold window on the last tapped object
constants.unit: updates of contact, lower bound inclusive, per update, rate unverified

constants.name: End of the hold window on the last tapped object
constants.unit: updates of contact, exclusive upper bound, per update, rate unverified

constants.name: Follow progress below which the character counts as stuck
constants.unit: world units of distance change per update, per update, rate unverified

constants.name: Stuck updates before a follow order is dropped
constants.unit: updates, per update, rate unverified

cards.name: Nearest touchable body under the stylus
cards.summary: The stylus picks the nearest qualifying actor whose projected hit body covers the touch point, not the first match in the actor table
cards.behavior: The pick scans the whole actor table and keeps the closest qualifying hit instead of stopping at the first. A candidate must be alive, pass an actor-specific eligibility test, have a touchable flag set on the actor or enabled by the current mode, and have its hit body touched by the stylus. Distance is the full three-dimensional distance from the actor to the player, so of two overlapping bodies the one nearer the player wins. The touch test lifts the hit body centre by the body size and passes that size as the on-screen tolerance, so the screen-space target covers a circle of roughly the body size around the lifted centre. The scan returns nothing when a global enable value is zero. The exact meaning of the eligibility and flag fields is not named in the source.

cards.name: Stylus stroke to sword swing class
cards.summary: A stroke must travel 10 pixels, and its direction against the facing picks one of four swing classes; fast strokes take a side class directly.
cards.behavior: Attacks are recognised from the shape of a stylus stroke on release. The stroke is accepted when the contact has just ended and lasted under 21 updates, or when a fast-motion flag is set and the slow duration is over 21. The stroke vector runs from the fast-drag point to the last point and must be at least 10 pixels long; when an unnamed flag is set the minimum is 20 pixels. If stylus speed is above 0.5 per update the swing is the fast variant and the sign of the stroke angle relative to the stroke heading picks the left or right class. Otherwise the stroke direction is compared with the heading recorded for the stroke: more than 135 degrees to either side gives class 0, 45 to 135 degrees on the positive side gives class 1, 45 to 135 on the negative side gives class 2, and within 45 degrees gives class 3. When the stylus stayed within 10 pixels of the character the class is 0 and the angle from the start of the drag is used.

cards.name: Aim point for boomerang, bow, hammer and rope
cards.summary: A held stylus produces an aim vector capped at 4 world units and a second aim point capped at an 8 unit parameter; the last aim point is kept after the stylus lifts
cards.behavior: Aimed items read an aim instead of turning the character toward the stroke. The short aim starts once the touch has lasted 16 updates: the stylus world offset from the screen centre becomes the aim vector, and its length is clamped to 4 world units, so a stylus at the screen edge cannot aim arbitrarily far. Before the 16-update hold, if the stylus is closer to the character than 24 pixels the aim point collapses onto the character, and otherwise it follows the stylus. A second aim point is built by a helper with an 8 world unit parameter that appears to cap its reach; the result is stored while the stylus is down and returned unchanged after the stylus lifts, so the item does not snap back at the end of a stroke. A helper that positions the companion passes the touch height plus 4.2 world units. Which items use which form is not shown here.

constants.name: Hold time before the stylus drives the aim
constants.unit: updates of contact, per update, rate unverified

constants.name: Aim direction length cap
constants.unit: world units, vector length clamp while the stylus is held, per update, rate unverified

constants.name: Stylus distance under which the aim collapses onto the character
constants.unit: pixels between stylus and character, per update, rate unverified

constants.name: Second aim point reach parameter
constants.unit: world units, helper parameter (cap interpretation unverified)

constants.name: Companion point height above the touch point
constants.unit: world units added to the touch height

cards.name: Gravity, fall cap and floor snap
cards.summary: Actors accelerate downward by 0.0498 units per update, cap their fall at 0.5 units per update, then snap up to the map floor.
cards.behavior: When the gravity step runs, the actor vertical velocity loses 0.0498 world units per update and the downward speed is then clamped at 0.5 world units per update, so from rest the cap is reached in about ten updates. Both values are per-actor fields initialised to these defaults in the constructor, so a floating or flying body only changes those two fields. The floor snap is a separate step: it asks the map for the floor height using the current and the previous position, and when the actor is at or below that height it is lifted to it and the call reports contact. How the map combines the two positions is not shown in this source.

constants.name: Default downward acceleration
constants.unit: world units per update squared, per update, rate unverified

constants.name: Default fall speed cap
constants.unit: world units per update, per update, rate unverified

cards.name: Cylinder bodies and contact reach
cards.summary: Bodies are upright cylinders whose single size value is radius and height, half a world unit by default, against a one-unit player radius.
cards.behavior: Collision bodies are upright cylinders described by one size value that serves as both radius and height. A negative size marks an empty body that never collides. The body has its own offset from the owner origin, which is rotated with the owner facing before overlap tests. A newly constructed actor starts with a size of 0.5 world units. The contact test with the player compares the three-dimensional distance between the actor and the player with the actor size plus 1.0; the source comment says the player body radius is 1.0 world unit. So a larger body is touched from further away, and the player counts as a wider target than a default actor.

constants.name: Default actor body size
constants.unit: world units, radius and height in one value, set at construction

constants.name: Player body radius used in contact reach
constants.unit: world units added to the actor size, per the source comment, checked once per contact

cards.name: Near and far actor classification
cards.summary: An actor within 10 units of the player on both horizontal axes is classed 1, any other as 2, and actors with certain flags are classed 0
cards.behavior: Actor activity is classified by distance instead of a streaming grid. A near check takes the absolute difference between the player and the actor on the two horizontal axes (x and z); the actor is near when both differences are at most 10 world units, so the near region is a square. The classification pass then stores a class value in the actor: 0 when any of five flags is set (two flags in a sub-record, two unnamed flags and the grabbed flag), 1 when near, 2 otherwise. What the three class values do afterwards is not shown in this file, so reading class 0 as forced active is an inference from the grabbed flag. The routine only assigns the class and neither moves nor deletes the actor.

constants.name: Near radius on each horizontal axis
constants.unit: world units, half-width of the square near region around the player, per update, rate unverified

cards.name: Shield arc and contact priority
cards.summary: The shield covers 90 degrees each side of the facing, and contacts resolve in the order sword, shield, hammer, roll.
cards.behavior: A block is angle based. The angle between the player facing and the direction from the player to the attacking body must be at most 90 degrees, and the shield volume of the equipped shield must also overlap the incoming body. So the guard covers the front half and nothing beside or behind the player. Contact resolution is a fixed else-if chain: sword overlap is tested first, then the shield, then the hammer, then the roll attack, and the first branch that matches produces the reaction and stops the chain. So one body gets at most one reaction per call, and a sword hit wins when the sword and the shield both overlap. Each branch fills its own reaction record. A block uses reaction level 2, raised to 3 when the wisdom companion level is at least 1.

constants.name: Shield half-angle around the facing
constants.unit: degrees from the facing direction, checked once per contact

constants.name: Companion level that raises the block reaction
constants.unit: level, checked once per contact

cards.name: Hit reaction level per incoming object
cards.summary: The source type of a hit maps to a fixed reaction level, from 1 for the first projectile type to 11 for any type not listed
cards.behavior: When another actor strikes a body, the reaction level is chosen from the type of the source actor rather than from its speed or mass. One beam-like projectile type gives 1, an arrow gives 7, a boomerang-like type gives 5, a hook type gives 8, and a group of four bomb-like types (including blasts) gives 6. A group of nine carried or heavy types, which includes two keyed item types, gives 10, one further type gives 4, and any other type gives 11. For the arrow and beam-like types the knockback direction is built from the sine and cosine of the source heading. For every other source it is the vector from the source previous position to the body position, so a rolling object pushes the body away from where it came from. The reaction level is passed to the hit handler together with the knockback record.

constants.unit: reaction index, dimensionless, per hit

cards.name: Knockback, damage window and respawn
cards.summary: A knockback call writes the vector straight into player velocity and turns the body opposite to it; death lifts the respawn point 0.6 units; health is clamped to zero and the maximum
cards.behavior: Damage does not blend with movement. The knockback call sets the damage state index to 2, copies the incoming vector directly into the player velocity and sets the facing to the direction of that vector minus half a turn, so the body faces back along the path it is pushed. The reaction level is stored for the animation choice. Minor damage uses a table whose defaults are a playback speed of 1.5, a start frame of 0 and an end frame of 10; front and back variants have separate rows, and a tuning loader can overwrite these rows, with the start frame ranged up to half the clip and the end frame from half to the full clip. Death is handled in a separate state: when it is in state 6 the player position is lifted by 0.6 world units and a respawn callback is registered. Health setters ignore the call while the player is invincible. A set or an add clamps health to between 0 and the maximum, and adding to a health of zero or less does nothing.

constants.name: Minor damage default end frame
constants.unit: q20.12 fixed point frames (0xa000 is 10 frames), default of an overridable tuning field

constants.name: Minor damage default playback speed
constants.unit: q20.12 fixed point multiplier (0x1800 is 1.5), default of an overridable tuning field

constants.name: Lift applied before the respawn callback
constants.unit: q20.12 fixed point world units (0x999 is about 0.6), applied once when the death state starts

constants.name: Facing flip applied on knockback
constants.unit: binary angle units (0x8000 is half a turn of 0x10000), applied once per hit

cards.name: Grab, push and throw an object
cards.summary: Pushing moves the player at most one twelfth of a world unit per axis per update toward a stand-off point; a drop leaves along the facing at 0.16 times the throw strength
cards.behavior: Object interaction is a state machine over approach, push, lift, carry and throw. While pushing, the object offset is rotated into the player frame and each of the two axes is clamped to one twelfth of a world unit per update, which sets the player velocity. On the forward axis the target is shortened by the object body size plus 0.4 world units so the player stands against the body. The approach test starts when the distance to the target is under its body size plus 3.5 world units. It then picks a variant by distance: a close band under 1.8 units that selects by facing difference, a middle band under 2.7 with a vertical tolerance of 1.2 units, and otherwise a far variant when a flag byte is zero. When one of two specific equipped items is active, the toss offset is 0.3 world units along the facing. Dropping a carried object gives it a velocity along the facing equal to the throw strength times 0.16.

constants.name: Push speed divisor
constants.unit: world units per update per axis is 1 divided by this value, per update, rate unverified

constants.name: Approach reach beyond the object body
constants.unit: q20.12 fixed point world units (0x3800 is 3.5), checked per interaction update, per update, rate unverified

constants.name: Throw speed per unit of throw strength
constants.unit: world units per update per strength unit, per update, rate unverified

constants.name: Pickup throw offset
constants.unit: q20.12 fixed point world units (0x4cd is 0.3), applied along the facing

cards.name: Hammer charge, animation timing and aim turn
cards.summary: A hammer charge counter of 40 counts down while held and sets a charged state at zero; a release passes the aim point and a charged flag to the map; the body turns toward the impact point in 45 degree steps
cards.behavior: The hammer item holds a charge counter initialised from a 40-update define. Each held update while the counter is above zero sets the charging state and decrements it, and reaching zero is reported. At zero the state becomes charged. A release hands the stored aim position to the map together with a flag that is true when the counter reached zero, and sets a separate countdown field to 4; reading that field as a recharge lockout is an inference. In the item state, a turn helper moves the player facing toward the stored impact point by at most 45 degrees (0x2000 binary angle units) per call.

constants.name: Charge time for the powered hammer
constants.unit: updates of the held item update, per update, rate unverified

constants.name: Countdown set on release
constants.unit: updates, per update, rate unverified

constants.name: Maximum turn step toward the impact point
constants.unit: binary angle units, 0x2000 = 45 degrees, applied per call, per update, rate unverified

cards.name: Hammer ground strike over nine tiles
cards.summary: A hammer release scans the impact tile and its eight neighbours, skipping map edges and floors that differ too much from the player height.
cards.behavior: A hammer release hands the impact position to the map, which scans a three-by-three block of tiles around the tile under that position. Coordinates outside the map width or height are skipped, so an impact at a room edge scans only the tiles that exist. A tile counts when the floor height differs from the player height by at most 0xcd in fixed point (about 0.05 world units), which keeps an impact from reaching things on a floor above or below, and a tile-data object exists there. The scan returns the value from the last qualifying tile, or -1 when none qualifies. In this reconstruction the floor height is read from the centre tile on every iteration rather than the neighbour being visited, which is probably a decompilation artifact, so treat the per-tile height test as unverified.

constants.name: Tiles scanned beyond the impact tile on each axis
constants.unit: tiles on each side, giving a 3 by 3 block per strike

constants.name: Floor height tolerance
constants.unit: q20.12 fixed point world units (about 0.05), compared with the absolute height difference, checked once per tile

cards.name: Per-room camera viewpoints
cards.summary: Each map ships a viewpoint table, and a per-slot id selects one, falling back to a mode default when the id is zero or missing.
cards.behavior: Camera framing is authored with the map rather than computed from the player. A map owns a table of viewpoint records, and two slots each hold a current viewpoint id, so two consumers can select different entries at once. A slot id of zero, or an id that is not found in the table, does not leave the camera undefined: a per-map default value is returned instead, which is 0x1c (28) in one game mode for non-zero results of a mode query and 0 otherwise. When the id is found, the record fields are copied into the caller structure, so switching rooms swaps entries instead of rebuilding the map.

constants.name: Viewpoint slots held per map
constants.unit: independent viewpoint ids, no timestep

constants.name: Alternate default viewpoint id
constants.unit: viewpoint table id (0x1c is 28), returned in one game mode, no timestep

cards.name: One-unit tile grid and per-tile floor height
cards.summary: A tile start is the map offset plus the tile index times 4096 in fixed point, so tiles are one world unit; a tile box runs from a height of -1.2001 up to the stored floor height
cards.behavior: Map geometry is queried on a square tile grid. A tile start is the map offset plus the tile index times 4096 in fixed point, and the tile end adds 4096 again, so a tile is exactly one world unit on each horizontal axis. Tile-based positions are centred by adding half a unit (0x800) to the start on both axes; that point is used for floor sampling and tile targeting. The box used for tile tests has a fixed minimum height of -1.2001 world units, not a value relative to the floor, and its maximum height is the stored floor height of the tile, so anything standing on that tile is inside its height range as long as its origin is above -1.2.

constants.name: Tile size
constants.unit: q20.12 fixed point world units (0x1000 is 1.0), static

constants.name: Tile centre offset
constants.unit: q20.12 fixed point world units (0x800 is 0.5), added to the tile start

constants.name: Tile box minimum height
constants.unit: world units, absolute height of the box bottom
